input.quote: Such books and records shall be kept for at least three (3) years following the end of the calendar month to which they pertain, and shall be open for inspection by an independent certified public accountant reasonably acceptable to Corio for the purpose of verifying the amounts payable to Commerce One under this Agreement. Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year, at reasonable times and upon reasonable notice. Commerce One shall bear all costs and expenses of such inspection.
input.rationale: Section 4.4 is the only audit/verification right binding Corio (our party), and it substantially meets the preferred position: audits are limited to once each calendar year, must be conducted at reasonable times and on reasonable notice, may be performed only by an independent CPA reasonably acceptable to Corio, and Commerce One bears all costs unless an underpayment exceeding 5% is found. There is no right of direct or remote access to Corio systems — only books and records relating to amounts payable — so no walk-away trigger. Minor points short of preferred wording, noted but not redlined: notice is "reasonable" rather than a fixed 30 (or fallback 15) days and in writing, and the auditor is not expressly stated to be bound by confidentiality obligations.
